versions.text: Verify that there is a primary and emergency (secondary) method to provide directional control during ground operations of the air vehicle for all the operational missions and flight configurations. DoD/MIL Doc: JSSG-2009 Appendix A: A.3.4.1.4.2/A.4.4.1.4.2 Directional control; and A.3.4.1.4.3/A.4.4.1.4.3 Emergency directional control AFGS-87139: 3.2.5.1 General; 3.2.5.2 Nose gear steering system MIL-S-8812 FAA Doc: 14CFR reference: 23.45, 23.497, 23.499, & 23.745

Criterion: Verify that there is a primary and emergency (secondary) method to provide directional control during ground operations of the air vehicle for all operational missions and flight configurations. Standard: Ground directional control of the air vehicle is maintained at all times during ground operations, including single point failure conditions. Systems that affect directional control of the air vehicle may include steering, brakes, flight control surfaces, and propulsion. Method of Compliance: Verification methods include analyses, tests and demonstrations. The FMECA identifies single point failure conditions and degraded modes of operation. Ground and simulator testing verifies that the directional control system functions safely in degraded and normal modes. Air vehicle checkouts indicate proper functioning of the primary, secondary and emergency directional control systems. Air vehicle ground and flight testing verifies safe operation of the primary, secondary and emergency directional control systems. References: JSSG-2009: A.3.4.1.4.2, A.4.4.1.4.2 Directional control; A.3.4.1.4.3, A.4.4.1.4.3 Emergency directional control AFGS-87139: 3.2.5.1 General; 3.2.5.2 Nose gear steering system MIL-S-8812 14 CFR 23.45, 23.497, 23.499, 23.745

Standard: Ground directional control of the air vehicle is maintained at all times, including under single point failure conditions. The primary and alternate (secondary or emergency) systems will provide continued directional control of the air vehicle during ground operations. Systems that impact directional control of the air vehicle include steering, brakes, flight control surfaces, and propulsion. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Review of the steering and brake systems' FMECA verifies that single point failure conditions and degraded modes of operation are identified, and mitigations are in place to allow continued directional control. Test.
  (1) Lab test: Conduct simulator testing to verify that the directional control system functions in normal and degraded modes.
  (2) Ground test: Conduct ground demonstration to verify proper functioning of the primary and alternate (secondary or emergency) directional control systems. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
  (3) Flight test: Conduct flight testing to verify proper functioning of the primary and alternate (secondary or emergency) directional control systems.
